messages:
nina (marketing): ran a targeted spike test after the webinar signups — 1.8k leads/min for 3m. observed unexpected owner fallthrough and a few duplicates in SF. attaching quick notes.

ben (ops): duplicates + fallthrough usually means our enrichment webhook didn't return before claim TTL. what was the enrichment_timeout in the test?

nina (marketing): we used 900ms to mimic a third-party vendor. in prod the consumer uses 1.2s. at 900ms fallthrough ≈ 9%. at 1.2s it fell to ~3.2%.

tori (growth): 9% is rough for a webinar. any pattern on which campaigns triggered it? high-utm_campaign ones?

nina (marketing): yes, the webinar campaign with heavy utm params and extra enrichment fields (company_size, role, timezone) hit the slow path.

kai (sales-ops): can we avoid fallthrough by deferring assignment until enrichment completes for flagged campaigns? maybe a soft-hold instead of immediate RR.

ben (ops): current claim logic: 
```
startClaim() -> triggerEnrichment() -> if (!enrichment.done && now - start > ENR_TTL) fallbackToDefaultOwner()
```
We could change to: if enrichment pending and queue_depth_high then routeToWarmPool() else wait up to X ms.

ben (ops): proposed params from the test: 
- enrichment_ttl_ms: 1200 default
- campaign_flag.high_throughput: true
- soft_hold_ms: 350 when queue_depth > 40
- warm_pool_owner: "inbound-warm-standby"

tori (growth): +1 for campaign_flag. We can set campaign.metadata.high_throughput on webinar templates. Then marketing can toggle per event.

kai (sales-ops): sample SF mapping rule I'll add: 
```
WHEN campaign.metadata.high_throughput = true AND lead.source = 'webinar' THEN owner = 'inbound-warm-standby'
ELSE normal_round_robin()
```

nina (marketing): other mitigations: 1) increase enrichment timeout for plugin-based vendors during campaign windows, 2) add a dashboard tile for "hand-off fallthrough % by campaign", 3) add an ops runbook for enabling warm pool and running a smoke spike.

ben (ops): I'll open a small PR to: add soft_hold behavior to claim worker, instrument queue_depth metric, and add a feature flag for warm-pool routing. plan: review today, staging canary tomorrow (10% traffic) with a 15m window.

deploy-bot: deploy plan queued by ben with tag: inbound-warmpool-2026-03-23. rollout policy: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks (fallthrough_rate < 2% for canary).

tori (growth): ETA on SF rule? want that in place before we flip feature flag.

kai (sales-ops): I'll PR the rule + update campaign template docs by EOD. also will add a quick checklist to onboarding doc for event producers.

ben (ops): followups: ADD metric: enrichment_queue_depth, ADD alert: enrichment_queue_depth > 60 for 2m, ADD dashboard: fallthrough_rate per campaign. I'll tag eng-infra for metrics quota.

nina (marketing): awesome. please add a step in the campaign runbook: "if fallthrough > 2% during spike -> enable warm-pool + increase enrichment_ttl to 1.5s".

ben (ops): agreed. one more note: avoid long holds for paid leads — warm-pool owners should be SDRs with tight SLAs. marketing to confirm which streams get warm-pool.

tori (growth): marketing confirmed: webinar signups and paid ad leads get warm-pool. I'll update the campaign list.

nina (marketing): thanks all. logging this thread + test outputs into the inbound-routing runbook. will follow up with the graphs and the exact PR link. :party-parrot:
